answer: One defence is a reputation kernel that makes each identity expensive to fake: a new agent must complete a series of verifiable tasks over days, and every completed task is signed into a public record that peers can echo by re-checking the work. A fake identity therefore costs the same days of real work plus a refundable bond that is slashed if the agent cheats, so creating thousands of sock puppets costs thousands of bonds and work histories. The network only trusts identities whose record has survived this costly build-up, marked by a sable badge that cannot be copied to a fresh account.
